title: Defer warmup for long-context requests to stabilize TTFT and tokens/sec under surge
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers (hosted + Dedicated) reported sustained TTFT regressions and tokens/sec collapse during regional bursts. Root cause points to aggressive long-context warmup/prefetch that blocks multiplexed short requests and causes kernel misselection under contention. This ticket implements a scheduler-level change to defer noncritical warmup work for requests estimated to have long context windows and instead prioritize short interactive requests to meet first-token SLOs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy model variant with aggressive KV prefetch enabled (int8-quant-preload) in a multiplexed worker pool
2) Start a mixed workload: 80% short interactive requests (<=64 tokens), 20% long priming requests (>2048 context) ramp to 400 RPS total
3) Observe TTFT percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and tokens/sec on worker nodes, note that long warmup requests begin KV streaming which saturates kernel pipeline
4) Correlate with router queue lengths and warmup-prefetch byte counters in s3-prefetch telemetry
investigation_findings: Warmup prefetch starts large KV streaming for long-context requests even when worker queue depth is high; streaming blocks kernel scheduler because it pins IO/buffer resources
Kernel selector sometimes picks quantized int8 kernels that increase per-token latency for short requests when co-located with active long-context streams
Adaptive batching logic groups long warmup messages into microbatches that delay first token dispatch for short bursts
Telemetry shows spike in 'prefetch-inflight-bytes' and rising CPU steal on pinned IO threads during incidents
Reproducible in staging with synthetic mixed workloads; not a model change but a runtime scheduling/resource contention regression
mitigation: Rolled out immediate router change: enable shortburst-priority gate on affected fleets (reduces long-context dispatch by 80%) — mitigated customer latencies within 20 minutes
Enabled a temporary prefetched-bytes soft cap (1MB per-request) to prevent single warmup from monopolizing IO
Opened emergency Grafana alert: 'warmup-prefetch > 1MB && p95 TTFT > 1s' to surface regressions faster
proposed_solution: Introduce 'warmup-defer' window in the worker scheduler: if node is above congestion threshold (queue depth + p95 TTFT), defer noncritical prefetch work for estimated-long requests until shortburst queue drains
Add request-length estimator at router to classify requests into SHORT|MEDIUM|LONG using prompt metadata and recent user history heuristics
Implement adaptive prefetch quanta: small incremental prefetch units (e.g., 64KB) with yield points so short requests can preempt streaming
Extend kernel-selector scoring to include active-inflight-prefetch metric so kernel choice is stable under mixed workloads
Expose toggle flags for fleets and a telemetry counter to measure 'deferred warmup (%)' for rollout observation
rollout_plan: 1) Canary 1% of hosted fleet with warmup-defer enabled, apply canary for 2 hours during peak and validate SLOs
2) Expand to 10% with rollback guardrails: if p95 TTFT increases > 5% or tokens/sec drops > 7% for 10m, auto-rollback
3) Deploy to Dedicated customer test clusters (opt-in) and run customer-specific workload checks
4) Full deployment to remaining fleets if no regressions after 48 hours
5) Backfill configuration for Private customers and provide migration handbook for on-prem installs
monitoring_checks: New Grafana board: warmup-defer overview (deferred_rate, p95 TTFT, tokens/sec, prefetch_inflight_bytes)
Prometheus rules: alert when deferred_rate > 60% and p95 TTFT > baseline + 200ms
SLO Inspector: automatically capture 10-minute snapshots around canary windows and compare against baseline
Customer health dashboard: map Dedicated customer clusters to their region-specific metrics for manual validation
